- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to revert; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above prior high or add mean-reversion decay.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., ±0.2), model often overestimates volatility; smooth forecast curve and reduce amplitude of swings.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is mildly negative (e.g., -0.1 to -0.3); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to early forecast points.
- When sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., >0.3), model often fails to capture sustained rally; extend upward trend slightly beyond observed peak or add 1–2% momentum buffer.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile (e.g., ±0.3 or more in 3–5 days); apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast variance by 15–25%.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate true price; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast, especially in first 10 days of horizon.
- Model often overestimates price in 30-day horizon when sentiment is positive but weak (e.g., 0.0–0.2); reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with true mean.
